unit.title: Measurement, Area and Perimeter
unit.blurb: Measuring length in centimetres, metres and kilometres, finding the perimeter of shapes, and finding area by counting squares.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Estimate and measure lengths in centimetres, metres and kilometres, and convert between cm and m.

O2.t: Find the perimeter of 2D shapes by adding the lengths of the sides.

O3.t: Find the area of 2D shapes by counting squares.

p: We measure short things in **centimetres (cm)**, longer things in **metres (m)** and long distances in **kilometres (km)**.
**100 cm = 1 m** and **1000 m = 1 km**. Line up the 0 on a ruler with the end of the object.
Measure from the 0 mark, not from the end of the ruler.

p: The **perimeter** is the distance all the way around the edge of a shape.
Add the lengths of all the sides: a rectangle 5 cm by 3 cm has perimeter 5 + 3 + 5 + 3 = **16 cm**.
A rectangle has 4 sides even if only 2 lengths are written.

p: The **area** is the amount of space inside a shape. We can find it by **counting squares**.
If each square is 1 square centimetre (**1 cm²**), a shape covering 8 squares has an area of **8 cm²**.
Mark each square as you count so you don't count it twice.
